messages:
jon: Hey folks — need a scrubbed SIEM export for vuln triage. We found suspicious outbound spikes from a prod host, asked the on-call analyst to deep-dive. Can we generate an export where PII is redacted and allow the analyst to decrypt for a short window? Ticket TKT-4732

maria: Short answer: yes, but follow the JIT unwrap + audit playbook. Default constraints: 48h max decrypt window, export TTL 7 days max with CISO signoff, and exported blobs must be scrubbed/tokenized.

jon: Got it. Who approves the decrypt? Is one approver enough?

maria: For privileged decrypts we require 2 approvers with entitlements: one security lead + one incident commander or infra owner. Approvers must be named in the ticket. Also add justification + affected host list in the ticket.

devon: Quick q — does the SIEM exporter need direct KMS key access? We prefer not to give the exporter service account kms:Decrypt.

samir: Don't give the exporter direct key perms. Pattern we use: exporter writes KMS-encrypted blobs to an encrypted S3 bucket using an exporter-wrapping-key. For JIT unwrap, a kms-proxy service (with limited audit-scoped access) performs the one-time unwrap when the ticket/approval is present. All unwrap requests go through the proxy which logs requester + ticket id.

alice-sre-bot: Ticket TKT-4732 created by jon. Please add approvers and expected TTL. See runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/security/jit-unlock

jon: Packaging/format question — what should the export contain? Raw events, or filtered fields only?

maria: Export must be field-filtered. Keep event-level metadata (timestamp, src_ip, dst_ip, process, host), but drop/transform user-identifiers. If a user id is required for triage, replace with a consistent pseudonym (HMAC or reversible tokenization stored only in the ticket vault). No plaintext emails/SSNs.

samir: Example scrubber config we use (simplified):

```
fields_keep: ["timestamp","src_ip","dst_ip","host","process","event_type"]
fields_drop: ["user_email","user_ssn","auth_token"]
pseudonymize: {"user_id": "hmac-sha256:KICKER_KEY_ID"}
output: "s3://redwood-siem-exports/TKT-4732/"
```

maria: Also add metadata tags to the export object: approvers, ticket_id, expiry_ts, justification_summary, scrubber_version. Those are critical for audits.

devon: For expiry — is 48h decrypt window the default? Can we shorten for high-sensitivity cases?

maria: Default decrypt window is 48h. For high-sensitivity items (PII risk, legal hold) we prefer 24h or less. Extension beyond 48h requires CISO approval and a documented retention justification.

jon: What about local analyst downloads? Can they pull the blob to their laptop?

samir: No. Exports must be analyzed in a secured bastion or ephemeral analysis VM with enforced disk encryption and no external network egress. If an analyst must copy derived artifacts out, they need an export subset scrub review.

jon: Understood. I'll add the approvers to the ticket and request a 48h decrypt window, bastion analysis, and hashed user ids.

maria: Great. Can you also include the exact query used to extract the logs in the ticket? We need reproducibility for the audit trail.

jon: Added query in the ticket and set approvers: @maria and @devon. Ticket updated.

alice-sre-bot: Approver devon approved TKT-4732 at 3747002550. Audit entry created.

devon: Approved. I confirm exporter will use kms-proxy unwrap flow only. I also added the ephemeral VM label to the ticket.

samir: I'll wire the exporter to produce the scrubbed export path and call the proxy on approval. Proxy will tag the unwrap with ticket=TKT-4732 and expiry=3747171950 (48h).

maria: Action items: jon — confirm affected hosts + query (done). devon — ensure exporter runs field-filtering and writes to S3 path. samir — configure proxy unwrap and audit log. Security will run post-export validation script.

jon: Thanks all — closing loop when analysis completed.

maria: Quick note for postmortem: capture whether any redaction hits were ambiguous. If so, add an eval dataset to improve scrubber rules. :memo:
